headline: Zealand Pharma and Generate Biomedicines have agreed to use AI to develop protein-based obesity treatments in a partnership worth up to nearly $1.2 billion.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an announced AI-drug-design partnership in obesity, but most of the value depends on milestones that may never be reached.
importance_line: People with obesity and other metabolic diseases could eventually get new protein-based drugs designed with AI, and the deal shows drug makers paying for AI design platforms, but only the $30 million upfront payment is certain, no drug candidate has been chosen yet, and the rest depends on future milestones.
summary: Reuters reports that Copenhagen-listed Zealand Pharma and Generate Biomedicines, a company in Somerville, Massachusetts, announced on Tuesday 13 Oct a partnership to develop protein-based medicines for obesity and other metabolic diseases with the help of AI, in a deal they value at up to nearly $1.2 billion. Generate gets $30 million at signing and up to $35 million for early lab goals reached before any testing in people, and could earn up to nearly $1.2 billion in payments tied to later development, approval and sales targets; Generate runs the research until a lead drug candidate is picked, and Zealand then takes over clinical trials, regulatory filings and bringing any drug to market.
notes: Reuters original blocked (HTTP 401); the text is Reuters's, read at Yahoo Finance. "Copenhagen-listed" is taken from the ZEAL.CO ticker shown on that page.
